selected_problem: Fresh-main inspection exposed the rollback-side twin of the just-closed apply defect: ChangesetStore.rollback checked a path and immediately restored it before checking the next path. A conflict on a later rollback path could therefore happen after an earlier path had already been restored, leaving a partially rolled-back workspace while the changeset remained APPLIED.

decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt is claimed. The committed DWAC North Star and four-mode router source contracts were replayed against fresh canonical code evidence; the rollback-side partial-mutation defect is narrow, central, evidence-rich, and directly adjacent to the previous apply-side closure.

code_reality: core/changesets.mjs rollback iterated reversed changes, checked each postimage, and restored that path immediately.
If a later rollback path had diverged after apply, an earlier path could already have been restored before ROLLBACK_CONFLICT was raised.
tests/changesets.test.mjs covered a single-file rollback conflict but did not prove all-path rollback preflight before the first restore.
The existing postimage hashes, WorkspaceService stat/write/remove operations, reverse rollback order, and receipt model are reused; no new transaction architecture is introduced.
changes: ChangesetStore.rollback now preflights every rollback path against the expected applied postimage before performing the first restore.
Only after all rollback preflight checks pass does the existing reverse restore loop run.
A regression test edits the later-checked rollback path after apply and proves ROLLBACK_CONFLICT leaves every earlier path in its applied state and the changeset APPLIED.

verification.evidence: With only the new regression test added to the previous main implementation, b.txt was restored to old-b before a.txt raised ROLLBACK_CONFLICT.

truth_boundaries: This closes deterministic postimage-conflict partial rollback; it does not claim filesystem-level crash atomicity or compensation for arbitrary I/O failures during restoration.
Arbitrary complex repository synthesis remains UNRESOLVED and was not declared solved by this transaction-layer repair.
No GitHub Actions are intentionally triggered or rerun, no force push is used, and no credential, payment, formal Release, destructive, or irreversible external action is authorized.
